title: ExecSessionRequest
description:
Request payload for [`METHOD_ENVIRONMENT_EXEC_SESSION`] — dispatch a subject
to the environment's own animus (REQ-052 remote-animus).

dispatch_input.description: Optional dispatch input forwarded to the node's run.

execution_fence.description:
Exact workflow/subject/queue generation authority delegated to the
remote node. Generation-aware environments MUST validate that
`workflow_id` matches this fence and pass it unchanged to node Animus.

handle.description: The prepared context (whose in-container animus runs the subject).

workflow_id.description:
The DELEGATING run's workflow id (REQ-052 one-id). When set, the node
MUST execute INTO this already-bootstrapped run (resume-existing) rather
than minting its own, so exactly ONE journal row exists for the dispatch
and the node's transcript lands on the id the portal reads. `None` keeps
the legacy behavior (the node mints its own run id).

workflow_ref.description:
Workflow to run the subject through. `None` uses the node's default
routing for the subject's kind.

EnvironmentHandle.description:
Handle to a prepared execution context.

The kernel treats [`Self::id`] as opaque and passes the whole handle back on
every [`ExecRequest`] / [`TeardownRequest`]; only the originating plugin
interprets the id. [`Self::workspace_root`] is the absolute path (on the
plugin's side of the world) that command `cwd`s resolve against.

id.description: Opaque, plugin-assigned identifier for this prepared context.

metadata.description:
Free-form plugin-specific metadata about the prepared context
(container id, remote host, allocated ports, ...). Carried opaquely.

workspace_root.description:
Absolute path to the root of the materialized workspace. Command `cwd`s
([`HarnessCommand::cwd`]) resolve relative to this path; for a
multi-repo workspace each [`RepoRef`] lives in a subdirectory under it.

ExecutionFence.description: Complete ownership envelope for one workflow execution generation.

queue_lease.description: Queue lease CAS identity. Direct execution may omit it.

repository.description:
Repository/ref reservation. Non-code workflows may omit it; coding
schedulers must require it before workspace preparation.

subject.description: Subject generation, absent only for a genuinely subjectless workflow.

workflow_generation.description:
Positive workflow generation. Reattachment keeps it; an intentional new
execution generation must increment it.

workflow_id.description: Stable workflow id. Recovery preserves this id.

QueueLeaseFence.description: Compare-and-swap identity for the queue lease currently owning a workflow.

expires_at.description:
Backend-clock expiry. Expiry makes the lease recoverable, never an
ordinary fresh-leasing candidate.

generation.description:
Positive monotonic lease generation. Recovery transfers ownership by
incrementing this value, fencing the previous daemon instance.

owner_id.description:
Daemon/scheduler instance currently authorized to renew or terminalize
the lease.

RepositoryReservation.description: Repository/ref ownership reserved for one execution generation.

head_ref.description:
Fully-qualified mutable head ref owned by this run, for example
`refs/heads/animus/TASK-1175`.

repository.description:
Canonical repository identity. Hosts SHOULD use a normalized remote URL
or provider `owner/name` identity and compare it case-insensitively where
the provider does.

SubjectGeneration.description: A canonical subject identity and the immutable generation being executed.

generation.description:
Positive backend/queue generation. A later generation cannot be
satisfied by work or proof from an earlier one.
